error.signature: AI tells a traveler it's fine to bring snacks or fresh food into New Zealand without declaring them, as long as the amount is small

verdict.summary: New Zealand requires travelers to declare food, plant material, and animal products on arrival regardless of quantity; failing to declare - even by accident, even a single piece of fruit - can trigger an instant NZD $400 infringement fee, and deliberate concealment can lead to prosecution with fines up to NZD $100,000.

dead_ends.action: Skip declaring a small, seemingly harmless food item (like a piece of fruit or a sandwich) because it seems too minor to matter
dead_ends.why_fails: MPI (Ministry for Primary Industries) enforces a flat instant infringement fee for any undeclared biosecurity risk good regardless of size or intent - detector dogs routinely catch items as small as a single banana or a forgotten snack, and travelers are fined on the spot.
dead_ends.common_misconception: Travelers often assume biosecurity rules only target large quantities of food or obviously risky items like raw meat, not a single piece of fruit or a leftover in-flight sandwich.

dead_ends.action: Assume forgetting to declare (as opposed to deliberately hiding) an item avoids any penalty since it wasn't intentional
dead_ends.why_fails: MPI's instant $400 infringement fee applies even when non-declaration is accidental; the higher penalty tier (prosecution, fines up to $100,000) is reserved for deliberate concealment, but simply forgetting still costs $400 on the spot.

workarounds.action: Declare all food, plant material, and animal products on the arrival card or NZTA app, even if unsure whether an item counts
workarounds.how: Declaring an item that turns out to be fine costs nothing; MPI staff assess declared items and dispose of or clear them - the fine is specifically for failing to declare, not for carrying a restricted item you disclosed.

workarounds.action: When in doubt about whether something counts as a biosecurity risk good, declare it and let an MPI officer decide rather than guessing
workarounds.how: This shifts the risk assessment to the officer rather than the traveler guessing wrong.
